section_summary: This section comprises official diplomatic and interdepartmental correspondence from May to October 1939 regarding reciprocal Federal income tax exemptions for non-diplomatic Japanese government officials stationed in or visiting the United States. Under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, the State Department certified to the Treasury Department that Japan granted equivalent tax exemptions to American officials, facilitating tax clearance and sailing permits for Japanese naval inspectors, language officers, academic researchers, and exposition commissioners. The records consist of notes between the Japanese Embassy and the State Department, executive correspondence between State and Treasury, and naval intelligence communications regarding Japanese personnel movements.

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption and departure facilitation for Sakae Yagi, who postponed his sailing and will depart New York for Europe.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy informs the Secretary of State that Sakae Yagi, a Japanese language officer from the Department of Education, postponed his scheduled April 27 departure from San Francisco due to government orders directing him to Europe. Mr. Yagi is now scheduled to sail from New York on May 20, 1939, aboard the steamship Columbus. The Ambassador requests that necessary steps be taken to exempt his official income from taxation and facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 103 regarding Sakae Yagi's Departure and Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary Messersmith transmits the Japanese Ambassador's note concerning Sakae Yagi's rescheduled sailing on the Columbus to the Secretary of the Treasury.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: The Department of State refers to earlier correspondence regarding the Federal income tax exemption of Sakae Yagi, a language officer of the Japanese Department of Education. It encloses a copy of the Japanese Ambassador's note stating that Mr. Yagi will sail from New York on May 20, 1939, aboard the Columbus instead of departing from San Francisco. The State Department requests that the Collector of Customs at New York City be appropriately instructed.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury regarding Sakae Yagi's Sailing from New York
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 103 regarding Sakae Yagi's revised travel plans and tax-exempt status.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 103 concerning the tax-exempt departure of language officer Sakae Yagi aboard the Columbus from New York. The note confirms that a copy of the Ambassador's communication has been forwarded to the Treasury Department. This ensures that the appropriate customs and internal revenue authorities will be notified of Mr. Yagi's exempt status prior to departure.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Sakae Yagi

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Iwao Yamawaki and Keinosuke Yamahata, officials sent by the Board of Tourist Industry for two American world expositions.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemptions for Iwao Yamawaki and Keinosuke Yamahata, officials of the Japanese Board of Tourist Industry. Both individuals were dispatched to the United States in connection with the New York World's Fair and the San Francisco International Exposition. Having arrived earlier in the spring, they are scheduled to depart from New York on May 13, 1939, aboard the steamship Europa, with all income derived solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 100 regarding Iwao Yamawaki and Keinosuke Yamahata

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for tourist industry officials Yamawaki and Yamahata.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull forwards Japanese Embassy note no. 100 to the Secretary of the Treasury concerning tourist officials Iwao Yamawaki and Keinosuke Yamahata. Invoking Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that Japan grants equivalent income tax exemptions to American nondiplomatic personnel. He requests that Treasury instruct its authorities to grant Federal income tax exemption on the compensation received by both officials.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Yamawaki and Yamahata
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that note no. 100 regarding Yamawaki and Yamahata has been referred to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 100 regarding the departure of tourist officials Iwao Yamawaki and Keinosuke Yamahata aboard the Europa. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been transmitted to competent United States authorities. This action is intended to secure Federal income tax exemption on their official Japanese Government compensation.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Yamawaki and Yamahata

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for landscape architect Nagao Sakurai prior to his departure on the Queen Mary.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents note no. 101 requesting income tax exemption for Nagao Sakurai, a Japanese government landscape architect. Mr. Sakurai worked in connection with both the New York World's Fair and the San Francisco International Exposition. He is scheduled to depart New York on May 10, 1939, aboard the steamship Queen Mary, having received his income solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 101 regarding Nagao Sakurai's Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for landscape architect Nagao Sakurai.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull transmits note no. 101 from the Japanese Ambassador regarding Nagao Sakurai's tax exemption to the Secretary of the Treasury. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that Japan extends reciprocal exemptions to American government employees. He recommends that Treasury issue instructions exempting Mr. Sakurai's official compensation from Federal income taxation.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Nagao Sakurai
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State confirms to the Japanese Ambassador that Nagao Sakurai's exemption request was sent to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State acknowledges note no. 101 of May 5, 1939, regarding landscape architect Nagao Sakurai's departure aboard the Queen Mary. The note confirms that the request has been submitted to competent United States authorities. This step was taken to ensure the exemption of his official earnings from Federal income taxation.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Nagao Sakurai

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges receipt of addresses for Japanese officials seeking Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges the State Department's letter of May 11, 1939. The letter transmitted addresses of Japanese officials stationed in the United States who had requested Federal income tax exemptions on April 29. Hanes expresses appreciation for the supplemental information provided.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Acknowledging Addresses of Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: The State Department advises that temporary visitor Yoshimoto Kobayashi obtain a sailing permit directly from the Internal Revenue agent in San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State replies to Japanese note no. 115 regarding Yoshimoto Kobayashi, Assistant Professor at Kobe University of Commerce, who plans to depart San Francisco on the Kamakura Maru. Because Kobayashi was admitted as a temporary visitor rather than on official Japanese government business, State advises an alternate procedure. He is instructed to present his passport in person to the Internal Revenue Agent in charge in San Francisco to receive a sailing permit.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Sailing Permit for Yoshimoto Kobayashi

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Assistant Professor Yoshimoto Kobayashi be included on the tax-exempt officials list.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador submits note no. 115 requesting income tax exemption for Yoshimoto Kobayashi, Assistant Professor of the Kobe University of Commerce. Admitted to the United States as a temporary visitor, Kobayashi is funded solely by the Japanese Government. He arrived in New York on May 11 and is scheduled to sail from San Francisco on June 24, 1939, aboard the Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 115 regarding Yoshimoto Kobayashi's Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges State's letter concerning the tax exemption and departure of student-official Eisaku Kiso.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State Department correspondence regarding Eisaku Kiso, who was sent to the United States for study. The letter notes the State Department's certification of reciprocal exemption under nondiplomatic status for Japanese officials. Hanes confirms that the matter is under careful consideration and advice will follow.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Eisaku Kiso

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges sailing details for Japanese naval personnel Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the State Department's letter of May 13, 1939, transmitting departure information from the Japanese Ambassador. The note details sailing dates and ports for Constructor Commander Masahide Iwasaki, Assistant Engineer Shigeru Nagashima, and Assistant Engineer Chuichi Itoh of the Japanese Navy. Hanes thanks the State Department for forwarding this departure data.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Naval Officers Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that Commander Ko Nagasawa's compensation is exempt from Federal income tax under Section 116(h).
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes responds to State's certification regarding Commander Ko Nagasawa, a Japanese naval language officer who departed Los Angeles aboard the Kamakura Maru. In light of State's Section 116(h) certification of reciprocity, the Treasury Department rules his official salary exempt from Federal income tax. Instructions have been issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue and the Internal Revenue Agent in charge in Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Commander Ko Nagasawa

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption for Juzo Ohtsuka, civil engineer of the Silk Conditioning House of Tokyo.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes informs the State Department that Juzo Ohtsuka, a civil engineer from Tokyo's Silk Conditioning House studying in the United States, has been granted tax exemption. Based on Section 116(h) reciprocity certification, his official compensation is held exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions were dispatched to the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse prior to Ohtsuka's departure aboard the Europa.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Juzo Ohtsuka

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that official compensation received by language officer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito is exempt from income tax.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes responds regarding Engineer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito, a Japanese language officer who sailed from Los Angeles on the Kamakura Maru. Following reciprocal certification under Section 116(h), Treasury determined his official compensation to be tax-exempt. Instructions confirming this status were communicated to the Collector of Internal Revenue in Los Angeles on April 22, 1939.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Lieutenant Takeo Ito

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms tax exemption under Section 116(h) for tourist industry officials Iwao Yamawaki and Keinosuke Yamahata.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes reports on the tax status of tourist officials Iwao Yamawaki and Keinosuke Yamahata following their assignment to the New York and San Francisco expositions. In accordance with State's Section 116(h) certification, Treasury held their official Japanese Government earnings exempt from Federal income taxation. Instructions were issued on May 8, 1939, to the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse ahead of their sailing on the Europa.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Yamawaki and Yamahata

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms the tax exemption of landscape architect Nagao Sakurai under Section 116(h).
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes informs the State Department that landscape architect Nagao Sakurai has been ruled exempt from Federal income tax. Sakurai had been assigned to the New York and San Francisco world fairs before departing aboard the Queen Mary. Instructions were transmitted to the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse on May 8, 1939.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Nagao Sakurai

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms tax exemption for Constructor Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto of the Japanese Navy Inspector's Office.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes advises that Constructor Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto, Inspector at the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York, has been granted tax exemption. Acting upon State Department certification under Section 116(h), Treasury ruled his official compensation exempt from Federal taxation. Appropriate instructions were issued to the Collectors of Internal Revenue in New York.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies the Japanese Ambassador that Treasury has approved tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese note no. 97 concerning Constructor Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York City. The Ambassador is informed that the Treasury Department approved his exemption from Federal income tax based on Section 116(h) reciprocity. Treasury has notified the Collectors of Internal Revenue in New York City accordingly.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Kitaro Matsumoto's Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure of naval clerk Umeji Kitagawa from San Francisco on the Asama Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador submits note no. 129 concerning Umeji Kitagawa, Clerk of Construction and Ordnance of the Naval Technical Department. Kitagawa, who had been included on the April 14 exemption list, is scheduled to depart San Francisco on July 10, 1939, aboard the Asama Maru. The Ambassador requests that United States authorities be notified to facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 129 regarding Umeji Kitagawa's Departure

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary Messersmith transmits notice of Umeji Kitagawa's departure to Treasury under prior Section 116(h) certification.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Messersmith transmits to Secretary Morgenthau a copy of the Japanese Ambassador's note regarding Umeji Kitagawa. Kitagawa is slated to sail from San Francisco on July 10, 1939, aboard the Asama Maru. Messersmith notes that reciprocal certification under Section 116(h) was previously provided on April 29.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury regarding Umeji Kitagawa's Departure
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 129 and confirms steps to facilitate Umeji Kitagawa's departure.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of note no. 129 concerning the scheduled sailing of Umeji Kitagawa from San Francisco on July 10, 1939. The Ambassador is advised that the note was transmitted to competent United States authorities. This notification is intended to facilitate Kitagawa's departure on the Asama Maru.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Umeji Kitagawa

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure from New York of Assistant Professor Keiji Sawada on the Kongo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that Keiji Sawada, Assistant Professor of the Tokyo School for the Blind, will depart the United States. Sent by the Japanese Government to examine educational and social facilities for the blind, Sawada is scheduled to sail from New York on June 27, 1939, aboard the Kongo Maru. The Ambassador requests that appropriate authorities be notified to facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 131 regarding Keiji Sawada's Departure

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary Messersmith forwards Keiji Sawada's departure details to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Messersmith forwards a copy of Japanese note no. 131 concerning Keiji Sawada's planned sailing on June 27, 1939, from New York aboard the Kongo Maru. The letter references previous State Department correspondence of April 29 containing a general list of officials. Messersmith reiterates that Section 116(h) reciprocity certification had already been executed.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury regarding Keiji Sawada's Departure
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that note no. 131 regarding Keiji Sawada was referred to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 131 regarding Keiji Sawada's upcoming sailing on the Kongo Maru from New York. The note confirms that the communication was transmitted to competent United States authorities. This step ensures proper facilitation of his departure without income tax impediment.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Keiji Sawada

subfiles.about: Treasury grants tax exemption under Section 116(h) to Japanese officials named on embassy lists, including Railway Department officials.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes reviews the lists of Japanese officials submitted under notes of April 14 and May 2, 1939, noting five officials of the Japanese Railway Department. In light of State's certification that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions, Treasury holds their official salaries exempt from Federal income tax under Section 116(h). Detailed instructions have been distributed to Collectors of Internal Revenue and Internal Revenue Agents in New York, Newark, Boston, Philadelphia, and Baltimore.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting General Tax Exemption for Listed Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies the Japanese Ambassador that Treasury granted tax exemptions to listed Japanese officials across multiple cities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese Embassy notes no. 76 and no. 95 transmitting lists of Japanese nationals seeking Federal tax exemption. The Ambassador is advised that Treasury accepted State's Section 116(h) certification and ruled their compensation tax-exempt. Instructions have been dispatched to internal revenue authorities in all cities where the officials are stationed.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding General Tax Exemption Approval

subfiles.about: Treasury reports that tax exemption instructions for Professor Eisaku Kiso have been mailed to New York and Philadelphia officials.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes provides an update regarding Eisaku Kiso, Professor at Otaru Higher Commercial School, scheduled to sail from New York on June 21 on the Europa. Letters have been mailed to the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse and to revenue authorities in Philadelphia confirming Kiso's tax-exempt status under Section 116(h). The revenue offices were explicitly alerted to his sailing schedule to facilitate clearance.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Eisaku Kiso's Exemption and Departure

subfiles.about: The State Department confirms to the Japanese Ambassador that Treasury notified customs and revenue agents of Eisaku Kiso's exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State replies to Japanese note no. 99 regarding Professor Eisaku Kiso of the Otaru Higher Commercial School. Quoting Treasury's communication of June 14, State explains that revenue collectors at New York and Philadelphia have been officially instructed on Kiso's tax exemption under Section 116(h). Specific attention was invited to his departure aboard the Europa on June 21.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Eisaku Kiso

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms that the New York Collector of Internal Revenue was instructed regarding Sakae Yagi's sailing on the Columbus.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes addresses State Department correspondence regarding Sakae Yagi's revised sailing from New York on May 20, 1939, aboard the Columbus. Treasury confirms that following a State Department phone call on May 10, written instructions were dispatched on May 12 to the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse. These instructions confirmed Yagi's tax exemption and facilitated his departure.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Sakae Yagi's Instructions

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms instructions sent to Seattle and San Francisco collectors regarding naval personnel Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes writes regarding the departure of Constructor Commander Masahide Iwasaki, Assistant Engineer Shigeru Nagashima, and Assistant Engineer Chuichi Itoh. Following Section 116(h) reciprocity certification, instructions were issued on May 23, 1939, to the Collectors of Internal Revenue in Seattle and San Francisco. The collectors were advised of their exempt status and their prospective sailing dates and vessels.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Naval Officers Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure of Harukage Ukawa from San Francisco on the Asama Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador submits note no. 136 regarding Harukage Ukawa, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commissioner in New York. Ukawa, whose name was listed on the April 14 exemption request, is scheduled to depart San Francisco on July 10, 1939, aboard the Asama Maru. The Ambassador requests that United States authorities be notified to facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 136 regarding Harukage Ukawa's Departure

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary Messersmith forwards Harukage Ukawa's sailing information to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Messersmith transmits a copy of Japanese note no. 136 concerning Harukage Ukawa, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commission at 120 Broadway, New York. Ukawa is slated to depart San Francisco on July 10 aboard the Asama Maru. Messersmith recalls that Section 116(h) reciprocity certification was previously provided in State's letter of April 29.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury regarding Harukage Ukawa's Departure
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 136 regarding Harukage Ukawa and confirms steps to facilitate his departure.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Embassy's note regarding the departure of Harukage Ukawa from San Francisco. The Ambassador is informed that the note has been referred to competent United States authorities. This action will ensure the facilitation of Ukawa's sailing aboard the Asama Maru.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Harukage Ukawa

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for language officer Yosiyuki Inouye stationed at Takamine Laboratory.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents note no. 137 requesting income tax exemption for Yosiyuki Inouye, Assistant Professor of Kyoto Imperial University. Sent to the United States as a language officer stationed at the Takamine Laboratory in Clifton, New Jersey, Inouye receives his salary solely from the Japanese Government. He arrived in San Francisco on April 20, 1939, and the Ambassador asks that US authorities be informed of his exempt status.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 137 regarding Yosiyuki Inouye's Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Assistant Professor Yosiyuki Inouye.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull transmits Japanese Embassy note no. 137 regarding Assistant Professor Yosiyuki Inouye of Kyoto Imperial University. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions to American personnel. He requests that Treasury grant Federal income tax exemption on Inouye's official compensation as a language officer.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Yosiyuki Inouye
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 137 regarding Yosiyuki Inouye's tax exemption request.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 137 concerning Yosiyuki Inouye, Assistant Professor of Kyoto Imperial University serving as a language officer. The note confirms that the request was transmitted to competent United States authorities. This was done to secure exemption from Federal income tax on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Yosiyuki Inouye

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges State's letter regarding Umeji Kitagawa's departure from San Francisco.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State's letter of June 16, 1939, regarding Umeji Kitagawa. The letter notes Kitagawa's plan to sail from San Francisco on July 10, 1939, and State's Section 116(h) certification. Hanes states that the matter will receive careful consideration and advice will follow.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Umeji Kitagawa's Sailing

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges State's letter concerning Keiji Sawada's departure from New York.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges the State Department's letter of June 17, 1939, regarding Keiji Sawada. He notes that Sawada expects to depart from New York on June 27, 1939, and that State certified reciprocal exemption under Section 116(h). Hanes assures that the matter is receiving careful consideration.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Keiji Sawada's Sailing

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges State's letter regarding Harukage Ukawa's departure from San Francisco.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Hanes responds to the State Department's letter of June 20, 1939, concerning Harukage Ukawa of the Japanese Financial Commission. He notes Ukawa's planned departure from San Francisco on July 10 and State's reciprocity certification. Hanes promises prompt consideration and advice.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Harukage Ukawa's Sailing

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for three newly arrived Naval Technical Department personnel.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador submits note no. 143 requesting income tax exemption for Japanese nationals attached to the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. The attached roster lists Teruo Mori (Assistant Inspector of Construction), Yoshio Miura (Assistant Inspector of Ordnance), and Mitsuo Okubo (Clerk of Construction and Ordnance). Their arrival dates in San Francisco and Seattle via the Asama Maru, Heian Maru, and Hikawa Maru are specified, confirming their salaries derive solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 143 and List of Naval Technical Personnel

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for naval personnel Mori, Miura, and Okubo.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull transmits Japanese Embassy note no. 143 and its accompanying roster of naval technical officials to Secretary Morgenthau. In accordance with Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies reciprocal treatment by Japan for American officials. He requests that Treasury grant income tax exemption on the compensation received by Teruo Mori, Yoshio Miura, and Mitsuo Okubo.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Mori, Miura, and Okubo
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State confirms to the Japanese Ambassador that note no. 143 was referred to competent authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 143 regarding the tax exemption of naval technical officials Teruo Mori, Yoshio Miura, and Mitsuo Okubo. The note confirms that their names have been transmitted to competent United States authorities. This action was taken with a view to exempting their official earnings from Federal income taxation.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Mori, Miura, and Okubo

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure from New York of Hiroshi Shiga of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents note no. 148 concerning Hiroshi Shiga, Technical Expert of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau of New York. Stationed in New York since February 1938, Shiga is scheduled to depart on July 7, 1939, aboard the steamship Europa. The Ambassador requests that United States authorities be notified to exempt his official income and facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 148 regarding Hiroshi Shiga's Departure

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull confirms telephone notification and certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Hiroshi Shiga.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull confirms a telephone message of June 29 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue and encloses Japanese note no. 148 regarding Hiroshi Shiga. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to American personnel abroad. He requests that Treasury facilitate Shiga's tax-exempt departure on the Europa on July 7.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Hiroshi Shiga
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Hiroshi Shiga's tax exemption request was referred to authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 148 concerning the departure of Hiroshi Shiga, Technical Expert of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau of New York. The Ambassador is advised that the note was transmitted to competent United States authorities. This step was taken to ensure his official income remains exempt from Federal income tax during his departure.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Hiroshi Shiga

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Hanes acknowledges State's letter regarding Yosiyuki Inouye's tax exemption request.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State's letter of June 26, 1939, enclosing note no. 137 regarding Yosiyuki Inouye. The letter notes Inouye's role as Assistant Professor of Kyoto Imperial University serving as a language officer, and State's Section 116(h) certification. Hanes promises that the request will be given careful consideration.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Yosiyuki Inouye

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges State's letter transmitting the tax exemption request for Mori, Miura, and Okubo.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges receipt of State's letter of July 5, 1939, enclosing Japanese note no. 143 and its roster of naval officials. The letter confirms receipt of the exemption request covering Teruo Mori, Yoshio Miura, and Mitsuo Okubo. Treasury assures the State Department that the matter will be reviewed carefully and an update provided.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Mori, Miura, and Okubo

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges State's letter regarding Hiroshi Shiga's tax exemption and departure.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges State's letter of July 5, 1939, regarding Hiroshi Shiga of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. The communication notes Shiga's pending departure from New York aboard the Europa and State's reciprocity certification under Section 116(h). Treasury confirms that the case will receive careful consideration.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Hiroshi Shiga

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Assistant Professor Yosiyuki Inouye.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury refers to State's letter of June 26 regarding Yosiyuki Inouye, Assistant Professor of Kyoto Imperial University. In view of State's certification under Section 116(h), Treasury holds Inouye's official compensation exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions have been issued to the Collectors of Internal Revenue at Newark, New Jersey, and the New York Customhouse.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Yosiyuki Inouye

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies the Japanese Ambassador that Treasury has approved tax exemption for Yosiyuki Inouye.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State replies to note no. 137 regarding language officer Yosiyuki Inouye of Kyoto Imperial University. The Ambassador is informed that the Treasury Department ruled Inouye's official earnings exempt from Federal income tax under Section 116(h). Appropriate instructions have been forwarded to the Collectors of Internal Revenue in Newark and New York City.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Yosiyuki Inouye's Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Treasury reports that the New York Collector was instructed regarding Keiji Sawada's exemption and sailing on the Kongo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury reports on the status of Keiji Sawada of the Tokyo School for the Blind. Treasury confirms that the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse had been furnished the general exemption list on May 24. Furthermore, on June 26, the Collector was specifically notified of Sawada's sailing aboard the Kongo Maru on June 27, ensuring compliance clearance.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Keiji Sawada's Tax Clearance

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms that the San Francisco Collector was notified of Harukage Ukawa's exemption and sailing on the Asama Maru.
subfiles.from: Herbert E. Gaston, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Herbert E. Gaston provides an update concerning Harukage Ukawa of the Japanese Financial Commission. Treasury confirms that on June 29, 1939, the Collector of Internal Revenue in San Francisco was advised of Ukawa's exempt status. Specific attention was directed to his scheduled departure on the Asama Maru on July 10.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Harukage Ukawa's Departure

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms that the San Francisco Collector was notified of Umeji Kitagawa's exemption and departure on the Asama Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury reports regarding Umeji Kitagawa of the Naval Technical Department. Treasury confirms that on June 29, 1939, the Collector of Internal Revenue in San Francisco was instructed regarding his official tax exemption under Section 116(h). The Collector's attention was specifically directed to Kitagawa's departure aboard the Asama Maru on July 10.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Umeji Kitagawa's Departure

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador submits complete records of all non-diplomatic and non-consular Japanese government employees in the United States.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents note no. 175 in response to the Secretary of State's circular note to Chiefs of Mission dated March 30, 1939. The Ambassador forwards official records of all officers and employees of the Japanese Government in the United States other than diplomatic and consular officers. This comprehensive filing provides the State Department with official documentation on all non-diplomatic personnel.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 175 Transmitting Records of Non-Diplomatic Personnel

subfiles.about: Treasury confirms that instructions were sent to the New York Collector regarding Hiroshi Shiga's departure on the Europa.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury writes regarding Hiroshi Shiga, Technical Expert of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. Treasury confirms that Shiga was covered under the general Section 116(h) exemption instructions issued on May 24. Following State's phone call of June 29, a supplemental letter was mailed to the New York Customhouse ensuring his tax-free sailing on the Europa on July 7.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department regarding Hiroshi Shiga's Departure Clearance

subfiles.about: Treasury rules that naval technical officials Mori, Miura, and Okubo are exempt from Federal income tax under Section 116(h).
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury responds to State's letter of July 5 regarding Teruo Mori, Yoshio Miura, and Mitsuo Okubo of the Navy Technical Department. Based on State's Section 116(h) reciprocity certification, Treasury holds their official salaries exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions have been issued to Collectors of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse, San Francisco, and Seattle.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter to State Department Granting Tax Exemption to Mori, Miura, and Okubo

subfiles.about: The State Department informs the Japanese Ambassador of approved tax exemption for naval personnel Mori, Miura, and Okubo.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese note no. 143 regarding the tax exemption of naval technical officials Teruo Mori, Yoshio Miura, and Mitsuo Okubo. The Ambassador is notified that the Treasury Department ruled their official salaries exempt from Federal income tax under Section 116(h). Instructions have been communicated to the Collectors of Internal Revenue in New York, San Francisco, and Seattle.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Mori, Miura, and Okubo's Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: The U.S. Naval Attaché in Tokyo reports three Japanese naval personnel sailing on the Taiyo Maru for the New York inspector's office.
subfiles.summary: The United States Naval Attaché in Tokyo sends a confidential telegram to the Chief of Naval Operations (OPNAV), copied to naval districts 11, 12, and 14. The telegram reports that Engineer Commander Kanhe Yatsugi, Paymaster Commander Tokuzi Taira, and clerk Goro Shimamaru are aboard the Taiyo Maru en route to the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. The message tracks incoming Japanese naval personnel assigned to technical inspection duties.
subfiles.title: Naval Attaché Tokyo Telegram on Japanese Naval Officers En Route to New York

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador gives notice of the departure from Seattle of naval aeronautics inspector Takeo Horiuchi on the Hiei Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents note no. 231 concerning Takeo Horiuchi, Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of the Department of Naval Aeronautics stationed at 1 Madison Avenue, New York City. Having arrived in the United States in April 1938, Horiuchi is scheduled to sail from Seattle on October 13, 1939, aboard the steamship Hiei Maru. The Ambassador requests that United States authorities be notified to exempt his official income and facilitate his departure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 231 regarding Takeo Horiuchi's Departure

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull confirms telephone notification and certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Takeo Horiuchi.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull confirms a telephone message of October 4 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue and encloses Japanese note no. 231 regarding Takeo Horiuchi. Pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that Japan extends reciprocal exemptions to American government personnel. He recommends that Treasury issue appropriate instructions to ensure Horiuchi's tax-exempt departure from Seattle on the Hiei Maru.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Takeo Horiuchi
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Takeo Horiuchi's exemption was referred to competent authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 231 regarding Takeo Horiuchi, Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of the Department of Naval Aeronautics. The note confirms that his scheduled sailing from Seattle on the Hiei Maru was immediately brought to the attention of competent United States authorities. This step was taken to ensure his official compensation remains exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: State Department Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Takeo Horiuchi

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for naval aeronautics inspector Takeo Kimura stationed in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador submits note no. 247 requesting income tax exemption for Takeo Kimura, Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of the Department of Naval Aeronautics. Kimura is stationed at the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office at 1 Madison Avenue in New York City, with salary derived solely from the Japanese Government. Having arrived in San Francisco on September 20, 1939, aboard the Tatsuta Maru, the Ambassador requests that appropriate US authorities be notified of his exempt status.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 247 regarding Takeo Kimura's Tax Exemption
